info.name: SpendWise Security
info.description: Security test round for the Docker Compose stack. Run the folders in order with the Collection Runner (or one by one). Every request asserts its expected status; failures name the control that did not hold. Log, database, Vault, gRPC and Kafka checks that Postman cannot do are in docs/security/security-test-plan.md. DEV ONLY: passwords and secrets below are the dev realm's.

item.name: 1 · Seed data (gateway)
item.description: Provisions both profiles, creates a category (admin) and one transaction owned by alice. The transaction POST is a bearer request without any CSRF header: bearer clients are exempt from CSRF by design.

exec: pm.test("status 200 - alice reaches user-service through the gateway", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("status 200 - bob reaches user-service through the gateway", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("status 201 - ADMIN may manage the category catalogue", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.test("status 201 - bearer write accepted without X-XSRF-TOKEN (CSRF applies to session cookies only)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: 3 · Authorization - roles and scopes (403)
item.description: Every service re-validates the token and applies `@PreAuthorize` (role + scope). 403 means "I know who you are, but you may not do this".

exec: pm.test("status 403 - CUSTOMER cannot list all users", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test('body is RFC 7807 problem JSON', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('status', pm.response.code); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('title'); });
pm.test("status 403 - CUSTOMER cannot change the shared catalogue", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test('body is RFC 7807 problem JSON', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('status', pm.response.code); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('title'); });

item.name: 4 · Ownership - is this record yours? (IDOR)
item.description: The owner always comes from the token's `sub`, never from the request. Someone else's record answers 404, the same as a record that does not exist, so ids cannot be probed.

exec: pm.test("status 200 - owner reads her own record", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("status 404 - not yours = not found (logged as OWNERSHIP_CHECK_FAILED)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));
pm.test('body is RFC 7807 problem JSON', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('status', pm.response.code); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('title'); });
pm.test('no row belongs to alice', () => rows.forEach(r => pm.expect(r.userId).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('aliceId'))));
pm.test('alice\'s transaction is not in bob\'s list', () => pm.expect(rows.map(r => r.id)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('aliceTxId')));

item.name: 5 · Gateway edge controls
item.description: CORS allow-list, identity-header stripping, request size cap and security headers, all enforced before a request reaches a service.

exec: pm.test("status 403 - origin not on the allow-list", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test("status 200 - the SPA origin is allowed", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

pm.test('ACAO echoes the SPA origin with credentials', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Access-Control-Allow-Origin')).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('webOrigin')); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Access-Control-Allow-Credentials')).to.eql('true'); });
pm.test('identity comes from the token, not the headers', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('aliceId')));
pm.test("status 413 - max-request-size 1MB stops it at the edge", () => pm.response.to.have.status(413));

item.name: 7 · Data protection and hardening
item.description: Errors without internals, actuator locked down at the gateway and in each service.

exec: pm.test("status 400 - bad input is a client error", () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('body is RFC 7807 problem JSON', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('status', pm.response.code); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('title'); });
pm.test('no stack trace or class names leak', () => { const t = pm.response.text(); ['Exception', 'at com.', 'at org.', '"trace"'].forEach(s => pm.expect(t).to.not.include(s)); });
pm.test("status 400 - bean validation rejects it", () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test('body is RFC 7807 problem JSON', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('status', pm.response.code); pm.expect(b).to.have.property('title'); });
pm.test('no stack trace or class names leak', () => { const t = pm.response.text(); ['Exception', 'at com.', 'at org.', '"trace"'].forEach(s => pm.expect(t).to.not.include(s)); });
pm.test("status 200 - health stays public for probes", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("status is one of 401 / 403 - every other actuator endpoint is denied at the edge", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([401, 403]));
pm.test("status 403 - denied even for ADMIN at the edge", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test("status 401 - operational endpoints need a token", () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
pm.test("status 403 - and the ADMIN role", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

request.description: GET, not POST, on purpose: security lets ADMIN through and the endpoint answers 405, so the check proves authorization without actually refreshing config (which would re-read Vault).

exec: pm.test("status 405 - ADMIN passes authorization; refresh itself only accepts POST, so nothing is refreshed", () => pm.response.to.have.status(405));

item.name: 8 · Service-to-service
item.description: The seed folder's transaction POST already exercised the Feign hop (transaction-service -> user-service with alice's token relayed). This folder exercises the gRPC hop (analytics-service -> budget-service, token in gRPC metadata). The negative gRPC checks need grpcurl: see docs/security/security-test-plan.md.

exec: pm.test("status 200 - analytics-service called budget-service over gRPC with alice's token", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("status 200 - bob gets his own dashboard", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('response does not mention alice\'s id', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get('aliceId')));

item.name: 9 · Token lifecycle (Keycloak)
item.description: Refresh-token rotation with reuse detection, logout, and the stateless-JWT trade-off: an access token issued before logout keeps working until it expires (5 minutes), which is why access tokens are short.

exec: pm.test('a new refresh token is issued (rotation)', () => pm.expect(body.refresh_token).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('aliceOldRefreshToken')));
pm.test("status 400 - a used refresh token is dead (revokeRefreshToken, max reuse 0)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test("status 400 - no session, no new tokens", () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));
pm.test("status 200 - stateless JWT: still valid until exp - the reason access tokens live only 5 minutes", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
